pert

/PURT/ - rhymes with alert · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Pert means flippant, bold; saucy.

Asked if she had practiced her recital piece, the nine-year-old gave a pert reply: 'Has the orchestra practiced theirs?'

Example

The new tour guide's pert asides — 'The castle is twelfth-century; the gift shop, regrettably, is not' — delighted the visitors and made her supervisor check the comment cards twice a day.

Pert is boldness at its lightest: quick, saucy, self-assured, and usually more charming than offensive. It shares a lane with cheeky and sassy; push the same nerve harder and you get brash, and push it past charm entirely and you are in the territory of this unit's brazen.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

sassy: Sassy is back-talk with attitude — a shade more defiant than pert, readier to test how much it can get away with. A pert reply stays light and self-assured, scoring its point and moving on; a sassy one leans on the disrespect a little longer.

cheeky: Cheeky means playfully impudent, banking on its own charm to be forgiven — the grin is half the act. Pert is cheek at its quickest and most polished: a pert reply is brief, saucy, and self-assured, in and out before anyone can object.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

meek: quietly submissive, swallowing every retort

respectful: careful to honor rank and occasion

Where it sits · how far cheek outruns charm

playful → pert → brash

playful vs. pert: Playful is milder than pert — pure fun, with no edge of impudence at all.

brash vs. pert: Brash is harsher than pert: pert banks on charm and stays welcome, while brash barrels past charm into pushy.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — pert: open, bold (from Latin apertus, 'opened')

Put it together: Pert is what remained when Old French apert, 'open, bold' — from Latin apertus, 'opened' — lost its unstressed first syllable on English tongues. The boldness of the open thing stayed: a pert answer is delivered with the visor up.

Use the root in a new word: aperture: The photographer widened the lens aperture — its opening — until enough light finally reached the film.

Strength Check

Word Choice

informal / affectionate

Pert is light artillery: quick, saucy replies that mostly amuse — a pert answer, a pert grin. Cheeky and sassy live on the same shelf. When the sauce stops being charming, reach for brash; when it turns shameless, that is this unit's brazen, a different weight class altogether.
